topic.para: &snapper; is set up as an undo and recovery tool for system changes. By default, the installer formats the root partition (/) of &productname; with Btrfs and enables snapshots for it. When calculating the size of the root partition, the installer reserves additional space for snapshots. By default, snapshots are disabled on partitions other than /.

warning.title: Enabling &snapper; after the installation changes the setup
warning.para: Enabling &snapper; in an installed system results in differences in the subvolume layout and variables, among other things. The setup then differs from the setup that this article describes.
We strongly recommend deciding whether you need snapshots before you start the installation.

topic.para: To install the system without snapshots, disable Btrfs snapshots for the root partition in the storage settings of the installer. In this case, you can still create snapshots manually. Keep an eye on the available disk space.

section.title: What does the default configuration include?
section.para: Certain directories are excluded from snapshots by means of subvolumes. For the list of excluded subvolumes, see . For detailed information about the types of snapshots, the time and occasions of their creation, see and .
Each partition or Btrfs subvolume has its own configuration file that defines the default behavior of &snapper;. These files reside in /etc/snapper/configs/.

You can roll back to an existing snapshot at any time by booting from the respective snapshot and making it active afterwards.

section.title: Subvolumes excluded from snapshots
section.para: When &snapper; is configured to operate on root, every Btrfs subvolume is excluded by default. The primary use case for snapshots is to roll back the system to a previous state. Therefore, snapshotting is disabled for certain subvolumes (directories).
The following list contains directories that are excluded from snapshots. Depending on your product, version, architecture and boot loader, not all of them may be available on your system.

listitem.para: A rollback of the boot loader configuration is not supported. The directories listed above are architecture-specific. The first two directories are present on AMD64/Intel 64 machines, the others on &aarch64;, &power; and &zseries;, respectively.
If /home does not reside on a separate partition, it is excluded to avoid the loss of user-created data on rollbacks.
These directories are used when manually installing third-party products. They are excluded to avoid uninstalling these installations on rollbacks.
The home directory of the &rootuser; user. It is excluded to avoid the loss of data on rollbacks.

This directory contains many variable files, including logs, temporary caches, third-party products in /var/opt, and is the default location for virtual machine images and databases. Therefore, this subvolume is created to exclude all of this variable data from snapshots and has copy-on-write disabled.

note.title: Temporary file systems
note.para: The /tmp and /run directories are not Btrfs subvolumes. They are mounted as tmpfs, which is kept in memory and not on the disk. Therefore, their content is never included in snapshots and is lost when the system reboots.
